people.name: Erik Reppel
people.role: Founder; x402 Foundation Technical Steering Committee
people.status: Left Coinbase in May 2026 to start a company; stays on the x402 Foundation steering committee and advises Coinbase on agentic commerce.
people.short: Created x402; left Coinbase to start a company, May 2026.
people.why: He connects machine-learning infrastructure with money that moves at internet speed. He joined Coinbase as an ML platform engineer in 2018 and later ran engineering at a startup. Back at Coinbase in 2025 as Head of Engineering for the Developer Platform, he co-authored x402, the open protocol that revived HTTP's long-dormant "402 Payment Required" so apps and AI agents can pay in stablecoins, launched in May 2025. In May 2026 he left to start a company of his own. He gave a forgotten status code a job.

people.name: Emil Ahlbäck
people.status: Left Lovable in 2026 after writing some of its first code; joined AI-agent startup Energy as founding engineer in August 2026.
people.short: Lovable's first engineer → founding engineer at Energy.
people.why: He connects open-source hacking with the prompt-to-app boom. He joined the team behind GPT Engineer as its first engineer, writing some of the first lines of what became Lovable when the project was rebranded in late 2024. Lovable went on to become one of the fastest-growing AI app builders. In 2026 he wrapped up his last day there, and in August he joined Energy, an AI-agent startup, as founding engineer. Line one, again.

people.name: Sid Bidasaria
people.role: Founding Engineer and Tech Lead, Claude Code
people.status: Founding engineer and tech lead of Claude Code at Anthropic.
people.short: Engineer #2 on Claude Code; created subagents.
people.why: He connects trading-floor engineering with the agents now writing code. Before Anthropic he built on Robinhood's options team and at Rubrik. At Anthropic he became engineer #2 on Claude Code, the terminal coding agent, and created subagents: specialist helpers that run in their own context windows with their own tools and permissions. Today he is the project's founding engineer and tech lead, and his personal site is built entirely with Claude Code. The agent that delegates had an author.

people.name: Fouad Matin
people.status: Works on Codex at OpenAI; led the first version of Codex CLI.

people.why: He sits where cloud security meets coding agents. He co-founded and led Indent, a startup built around time-bound, policy-based access to cloud infrastructure. In May 2024 he joined OpenAI, where he led the first version of Codex CLI, the open-source terminal agent. In May 2025 he announced its rewrite as a native Rust binary with tighter sandboxing, and he has spoken on keeping code-executing agents safe. The agent in your terminal had a security-minded first author.

people.name: Kathryn Tunyasuvunakool
people.status: Joined Isomorphic Labs as Principal Research Scientist in October 2026, after eight years at Google DeepMind.
people.short: Joined Isomorphic Labs, Oct 2026; ex-DeepMind AlphaFold.
people.why: She connects computational biology with the AI that reshaped it. She joined DeepMind in 2018 as a science engineer and worked on AlphaFold, comparing its predictions with lab structures in 2020, work that led to AlphaFold-Multimer. In 2021 she was lead author on the paper that predicted structures for the human proteome, and in 2022 MIT Technology Review named her an Innovator Under 35. In October 2026 she joined Isomorphic Labs as Principal Research Scientist. From folding proteins to finding medicines.

people.name: Da Huang
people.status: Left Google DeepMind for Discovery Loop in October 2026 after ten years at Google.
people.short: Left DeepMind for Discovery Loop, Oct 2026.
people.why: He connects a decade of Google machine learning with AI that improves itself. Over ten years at Google he moved from hand-tuning models to automated machine learning, the field of letting algorithms design and tune other models. On October 10, 2026 he announced he had left Google DeepMind to join Discovery Loop as a Member of Technical Staff, focused on recursive self-improvement: AI systems that help improve their own capabilities. From tuning models to models that tune themselves.

people.name: Konstantin Mishchenko
people.status: Left Meta in August 2026; joined Mistral AI's pretraining team in October 2026.
people.short: Prodigy and Schedule-Free optimizers → Mistral, Oct 2026.
people.why: He connects optimization theory with the brute work of training frontier models. After a PhD at KAUST and a stint at Samsung AI Center, he co-authored D-Adaptation and Prodigy, optimizers that cut out manual learning-rate tuning. In 2024 his Schedule-Free AdamW submission won the self-tuning track of the first MLCommons AlgoPerf competition, and that October he joined Meta as a research scientist. In October 2026 he joined Mistral AI's pretraining team, saying model quality now comes before papers. Less tuning, more training.

media.caption: Regularized Newton Method with Global O(1/k^2) Convergence (One World Optimization Seminar)

people.name: Josh Engels
people.status: Left Google DeepMind's AGI Safety team in August 2026 to join METR.
people.short: DeepMind AGI Safety → METR, 2026.
people.why: He connects interpretability research with independent oversight of frontier AI. In 2024 he was lead author, with Max Tegmark's group at MIT, on "Not All Language Model Features Are Linear", which used sparse autoencoders to find circular day-of-week and month features inside GPT-2 and Mistral 7B, published at ICLR 2025. He then joined Google DeepMind's AGI Safety team, working on scalable oversight. In 2026 he left for METR to study where misaligned behavior comes from and whether safeguards hold. Opening the black box, then auditing it.

media.caption: Sparse Autoencoders: Progress & Limitations with Joshua Engels

people.name: Isa Fulford
people.status: Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI; leads post-training work on Deep Research and ChatGPT agent.
people.short: Research lead behind OpenAI Deep Research.
people.why: She connects reinforcement learning with agents that do hours of work in minutes. At OpenAI she was a research lead on Deep Research, the browsing research agent launched in February 2025 and trained end to end on hard browsing tasks. That July she helped ship ChatGPT agent, which combined browsing, computer use, code and tools into one system, and she now leads post-training work on both. Forbes has profiled her among AI's rising builders. Quiet name, loud agents.
